thread:
Leah: Following up on the API migration RFC  proposing an "edge translator" shim at the ingress to accept legacy shapes and emit the new runtime contract. Opt-in via tenant flag. We need to decide streaming behavior and KV/cache key compatibility.
Arun: Agree opt-in. Big risk is streaming semantics: old clients expect chunked "content" frames, new runtime uses structured "delta" events. Do we reframe on the edge or convert inside runtime?
Noah: We prototyped a small translator in Envoy Lua that rewrites first chunk metadata and wraps subsequent chunks. Overhead negligible for median but p99 hit ~5ms when payloads are large.
Leah: Important: avoid double-serialization. If we reframe at the gateway we avoid runtime branching, but gateway teams will need to own tests and security reviews.
Vera: Also watch cache keys for prefix caching and KV-tokenization. If shim renames fields, cached keys for embeddings and prefix cache may miss. Need deterministic canonicalization function.
Arun: Suggestion: add header X-Compat-Translator: active and X-Compat-Mode: best-effort|strict so we can run best-effort by default and strict per-tenant. Best-effort forwards original with shim header on failure, strict returns 422.
Noah: Pseudocode I used in staging: 
```
if header == "X-Compat: legacy->new":
  if stream:
    read first frame, map metadata, emit new header-frame, then passthrough mapped frames
  else:
    try transform(body)
    if transform_error:
      if tenant_mode == strict: return 422
      else: add header X-Translator-Warning and forward original
```

Leah: Good. Telemetry we need: translator_invoked, translator_latency_ms, translator_serde_bytes, translator_miss_cache_count. Tag by tenant_id and request_route. Put traces into existing request trace IDs.
Vera: Ops-bot can create dashboards and alerts. Ops-bot: please add a steady-state alert if translator_error_rate > 1% across >5 tenants for 10m.
ops-bot: Added alert rule "translator_error_rate" -> notify on-call if >1% for 10m for >=5 tenants. Dashboard "Edge Translator - latency / errors" created.
Arun: One subtlety: function calling schema changed names for tool args. We must either polyfill arg names or add a compatibility wrapper in the tool registry. Otherwise downstream tool clients will break.
Noah: For tool args we can map harmless aliases, but avoid mutation semantics that change semantics. For ambiguous mappings, log a deprecation notice header X-Compat-Notice and preserve original payload in a tombstone header pointer to S3 if tenant requests debugging.
Leah: Security: no template eval or runtime code generation in transforms. Use a white-listed mapping table and deterministic rules. Audit all mapping entries before rollout.
Vera: Rollout plan: internal dev tenants (3) -> beta partners (10) -> 50 tenants -> broad. Canary metric gates: translator_error_rate, p99_request_latency delta, cache_hit_ratio. Rollback: flip tenant flag off or remove translator from edge.
Arun: For long term, if translator usage grows >20% of requests, we should consider upstreaming mappings into the runtime to reduce cross-team burden.
Noah: I'll produce an Envoy Lua reference and a C++ sketch for the gateway hook. ETA 72h for artifacts + perf numbers.
Leah: I'll own the migration playbook and doc the mapping whitelist and the strict-mode semantics. ETA 24h.
Vera: I'll coordinate security review and add RBAC for tenant flag toggle. Ops will run perf load to measure p99 impact.
Leah: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after artifacts. :white_check_mark:
